labels.label:
Connector - CSV file stored in AWS S3 to Snowflake

This connector extracts data from a CSV file in S3 and loads it into Snowflake. It infers the schema from the CSV and creates/updates the destination table, then truncates and reloads it on each run.

parameters.description: Leave this blank when using Session Token for your Authentication Strategy. When using KEY_PAIR, provide your Snowflake account name formatted as [organization-name]-[account-name] where data will be persisted.
parameters.name: Snowflake Account Identifier

parameters.description: Leave this blank when using Session Token for your Authentication Strategy. When using KEY_PAIR, provide the RSA private key used for authentication. The RSA key must be formatted according to PKCS8 standards and have standard PEM headers and footers.
parameters.name: Snowflake Private Key

parameters.description: Leave this blank when using Session Token for your Authentication Strategy. When using KEY_PAIR, provide the password associated with the Snowflake Private Key File.
parameters.name: Snowflake Private Key Password

parameters.description: When using Session Token for your Authentication Strategy, use your Runtime Role. When using Key Pair for your Authentication Strategy, use a valid role configured for your service user.
parameters.name: Snowflake Role

parameters.description: Leave this blank when using Session Token for your Authentication Strategy. When using KEY_PAIR, provide the user name used to connect to Snowflake instance.
parameters.name: Snowflake Username

parameters.description: Snowflake warehouse used to run queries when inserting data into the destination table.
parameters.name: Snowflake Warehouse

parameters.description: The prefix of the table in the destination schema where CSV data will be persisted.
parameters.name: Destination Table Prefix

parameters.description: The S3 bucket from which the CSV files should be fetched.

parameters.description: List of comma-separated object keys within the S3 bucket that contain CSV files to fetch, e.g. "file1.csv,file2.csv".
